 Judgment
The petitioner has filed the captioned writ petition, seeking to challenge the action taken by respondents in locking and sealing building No.18/1 in Amarambalam Panchayat.
The petitioner has sought for a direction to the 2nd respondent to remove the lock and seal and to permit the petitioner to occupy the building in question and to do business therein.

2. I have heard Sri.P.Samsudin, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Grashious Kuriakose,
the learned Additional Director General of Proecution 3. Sri.Grashious Kuriakose, would point out firstly that the building in its entirety has not been closed.

He would point out that only the room in question, wherein the disputed articles were kept,
was locked.

He further points out that the proceedings initiated on the basis of the seizure with reference to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, have already been finalised against the petitioner, imposing a penalty of Rs.5,000/-, which however, has not been paid by the petitioner.
Sri.Samsudin, on the other hand, would point out that, no such order has ever been served on the petitioner.
In any view of the matter, I notice that since the proceedings have already been finalised, this writ petition can be disposed of with directions.
i) The respondents to serve a certified copy of the order said to have been passed against the petitioner herein, as above, within a period of three weeks from today.

ii) The respondents to open the shop room in question forthwith, and the petitioner is permitted to occupy the same in accordance with law.
iii) Needless to say that the petitioner would be entitled to challenge the order said to have been passed against him, in accordance with law.
This writ petition is disposed of as above.
